# Poe2AiAccessor

[API index](../index)

Script-facing surface over the PoE2 AI behavior registry — `World.Ai` in scripts.

READ-ONLY: writing is the named per-behavior setters' job (`SetAutoFarm`, `SetVoidZoneTracker`,
... on the sandbox root), so there is no generic toggle here. Reads resolve through
[`Poe2Game::htn_manager`] into the registry methods on `Poe2HtnManager`, which hold the single
exhaustive match per question.

## IsEnabled

```typescript
IsEnabled(behavior: Poe2Behavior): boolean;
```

Whether `behavior` is currently enabled — the authoritative registry answer, `false`
when detached or the HTN manager is unavailable.
Reads the stored toggle, not current execution. Use IsActive to also require the global Automation gate.

**Example**

```ts
const followEnabled = World.Ai.IsEnabled(Poe2Behavior.AutoFollow);
```

**@keywords**

automation, follow, toggle, enabled, behavior

## Status

```typescript
Status(behavior: Poe2Behavior): string;
```

The behavior's live status line (its `Status()` seam), or a short explanation when the
game is detached / the manager is unavailable.

## IsActive

```typescript
IsActive(behavior: Poe2Behavior): boolean;
```

Whether `behavior` is currently derived-ACTIVE — the authoritative registry answer
(`IsActive == IsEnabled AND the global Automation gate is active`), `false` when detached or the HTN manager is
unavailable. Distinct from [`Self::IsEnabled`] (the raw stored intent): a behavior can be
enabled yet inactive because the global Automation gate is inactive.
Active does not mean the character is currently moving or executing a follow task.

**@keywords**

automation, follow, active, gate, behavior

## Reason

```typescript
Reason(behavior: Poe2Behavior): string;
```

The decisive REASON behind `behavior`'s current derived activation ("Automation inactive" when the
global Automation gates it off, "<Behavior> off" when its own intent is off, "<Behavior> active"
otherwise), or a short explanation when detached / the manager is unavailable. Pairs with
[`Self::IsActive`] and complements the behavior's own [`Self::Status`] activity line.

## Behaviors

```typescript
Behaviors: string[];
```

Names of every togglable behavior, straight from the single [`ALL`] table.
